plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a fixed 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack, with individually tunable thicknesses, can achieve the dual-band dichroic performance required for satellite quantum key distribution. The hypothesis draws on recalled thin-film design principles: high-index contrast pairs create broadband reflection bands, while thickness tuning can open transmission windows at target wavelengths. This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone, with no literature retrieval. What I would have wanted to look up: exact dispersion data for HfO2 and SiO2 at cryogenic space temperatures, typical deposition stress values for these materials, and published dichroic filter designs for similar wavelength splits.

routes.title: 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with thickness optimization and phase-jump repair
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually optimized thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high transmittance in the 1530-1565 nm telecom band and high reflectance in the 400-700 nm visible band, without requiring more than 30 layers or additional materials.
routes.design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Dichroic filters use alternating high and low refractive index layers to create constructive interference for reflection at certain wavelengths. The HfO2/SiO2 pair provides sufficient index contrast (~2.0 vs ~1.45 in the visible) to build broadband reflectors. Quarter-wave optical thickness at the center of the reflection band maximizes reflectance, but deviating from quarter-wave can open transmission windows at desired wavelengths. With 24 layers, there are enough degrees of freedom to shape both the visible rejection band and the telecom passband.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual thickness of each of the 24 layers (24 independent variables, range 20-400 nm per layer)
Global perturbation amplitude for optimization (fixed at 5 nm for this iteration)
Phase-jump repair: 10% of population receives stochastic thickness offsets of ±50 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain layer thicknesses within manufacturable range (20-400 nm)
Keep total layer count at exactly 24 (within 30-layer constraint)
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers is within the 30-layer maximum constraint
HfO2 and SiO2 are both depositable by ion-assisted deposition or sputtering
Individual layer thicknesses should remain above 20 nm to avoid pinhole defects
Thicknesses above 400 nm may introduce stress and adhesion issues
Uniform initialization weights applied across all 24 layers (no asymmetric weighting on specific layers)
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Alternating high/low index layers create photonic bandgaps where reflectance is high
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has refractive index approximately 1.9-2.1 in visible/near-IR, SiO2 approximately 1.45-1.47
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks centered at ~550 nm would give high visible reflectance but may not optimally transmit 1550 nm
Recalled knowledge: Non-quarter-wave thickness tuning can create transmission windows within a high-reflectance band
Recalled knowledge: 12 pairs (24 layers) is a common starting point for dichroic filters with moderate bandwidth requirements
Recalled knowledge: Gradient-based optimization with periodic large perturbations can escape local minima in multimodal thickness spaces
expected_advantages: 24 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band shaping
HfO2/SiO2 is a robust, space-qualified material pair with low absorption in both bands
Fixed topology with thickness-only optimization isolates the effect of geometric tuning
Phase-jump repair mechanism should help escape local interference minima that trapped previous iterations
5 nm perturbation amplitude provides more exploration range than 2 nm while maintaining convergence
known_risks: Uncertainty: Exact refractive index dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 at 1530-1565 nm - recalled values are approximate and would need to be confirmed from the material catalog datasets
Uncertainty: Whether 24 layers is optimal or if fewer layers could achieve similar performance with better robustness
Uncertainty: Angle sensitivity not explicitly specified in the original request - this design assumes near-normal incidence but satellite windows may see off-axis light
Uncertainty: The phase-jump repair with ±50 nm offsets may disrupt convergence if applied too aggressively; 10% population rate is a heuristic guess
Uncertainty: Starting thickness values from prior iterations may be in a poor local minimum; the phase-jump should help but success is not guaranteed
Known risk: Previous iteration 14 showed degraded performance (0.78 vs 0.93 in iteration 10); this revision attempts to recover the higher performance through modified optimization parameters
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer planar dielectric thin film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer materials alternate between HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with HfO2 at the air side. Optimize the individual thickness of each of the 24 layers to maximize transmittance in the 1530-1565 nm wavelength band while maximizing reflectance in the 400-700 nm wavelength band. Each layer thickness is an independent variable constrained between 20 nm and 400 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimization with global perturbation amplitude of 5 nm. Apply uniform initialization weights across all 24 layers (no asymmetric weighting on layers 3 or 6). Include a phase-jump repair step: at each optimization round, randomly select 10% of the candidate population and apply stochastic thickness offsets of ±50 nm to forcibly cross local interference minima before resuming gradient refinement. Total layer count is fixed at exactly 24 layers. Materials are HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only. Substrate is fused silica. Incident medium is air. Evaluate performance using frequency-domain plane-wave illumination at normal incidence.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation of control route with modified optimization parameters: reverted perturbation amplitude from 2 nm to 5 nm, decoupled asymmetric refinement weights to uniform across all layers, and added phase-jump repair mechanism with 10% population at ±50 nm offsets to escape local minima observed in iteration 14

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route used no retrieved literature and no method research, and was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 24 layers is the optimal count or if 20 or 28 layers would perform better - this route fixes 24 to isolate thickness tuning effects
The exact starting thickness values for optimization - using prior iteration results but these may not be globally optimal
Whether normal incidence is sufficient or if angle averaging should be included - the original request did not specify angle
The 10% population rate for phase-jump repair is a heuristic; the optimal rate is unknown without empirical testing
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all routes fail to achieve target_score above 0.80, the problem may require either more than 30 layers, different material pairs with higher index contrast, or a non-alternating layer sequence topology

expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should rise from iteration 14's 0.78 toward iteration 10's 0.93 range as the phase-jump repair helps escape local minima
valid_candidates should remain high (≥5) indicating the thickness constraints are not overly restrictive
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if the optimization is converging to robust solutions
thicknesses_nm should show variation across layers rather than converging to uniform values, indicating the optimizer is using the degrees of freedom
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau below 0.85 despite the phase-jump repair, suggesting 24 layers with this topology is insufficient for the dual-band requirement
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, reduce the phase-jump offset magnitude from ±50 nm to ±25 nm and continue
If tightest_margin falls below 0.3 for three consecutive rounds, relax the minimum thickness constraint from 20 nm to 15 nm and continue
If after 5 rounds the best_target_score remains below 0.80, stop and flag that the 24-layer alternating topology may be insufficient for this wavelength split

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
